papers.title: Your Agents Are Aging Too: Agent Lifespan Engineering for Deployed Systems
papers.innovation: Introduces the crucial concept of 'agent lifespan engineering,' shifting evaluation focus from initial performance to long-term reliability and degradation in deployed AI agent systems. This addresses a critical, often-overlooked challenge in maintaining operational AI agents.
papers.benchmarks: Critiques current day-one benchmarks as insufficient for assessing the long-term reliability and efficacy of deployed agents, implicitly calling for new longitudinal evaluation methodologies to track performance degradation and robustness over time.
papers.use_case: Essential for AI engineers responsible for deploying, monitoring, and maintaining long-lived AI agents in production environments. It provides a framework for anticipating and mitigating performance degradation, ensuring continuous reliability and trustworthiness of operational AI systems.

papers.title: Is Agent Memory a Database? Rethinking Data Foundations for Long-Term AI Agent Memory
papers.innovation: Proposes a fundamental rethinking of agent memory, moving beyond simple storage to a holistic data foundation. It emphasizes establishing correctness not just at individual records or embeddings, but across the entire memory system, crucial for persistent, reliable agents.
papers.benchmarks: Highlights the inadequacy of current paradigms in evaluating the holistic correctness and integrity of long-term agent memory, suggesting a need for benchmarks that assess how well memory supports learning across sessions, reduces context injection, and enables auditing.
papers.use_case: Critical for AI engineers designing the architectural backbone of long-running AI agents. This paper guides the development of robust, scalable, and auditable memory systems that enable agents to learn persistently, maintain context, and ensure decision-making integrity over extended periods.

papers.title: Personalizing Embodied Multimodal Large Language Model Agents over Long-term User Interactions
papers.innovation: Addresses the significant challenge of personalizing MLLM-based embodied agents. It moves beyond generic instruction following to enable agents to adapt to individual user preferences and specific real-world contexts over long-term interactions, which is key for practical utility.
papers.benchmarks: Implicitly argues for the need for benchmarks that can rigorously evaluate an agent's ability to personalize its interactions, understand nuanced user intent, and adapt to specific targets and evolving user needs through extended engagements in complex environments.
papers.use_case: Highly relevant for AI engineers developing user-facing embodied AI assistants, robots, or virtual agents. This work provides insights into building agents that can offer truly personalized and context-aware assistance, enhancing user experience and agent effectiveness in real-world, long-term deployments.
